idiom_name: class per table over std::vector<Row> (sqlpp11 for typed queries)
implementation_notes: C++ supplies the class and the container but not the record set: a Table Module is a class (or namespace) per table whose methods take and return std::vector<Row>, with the rows pushed into the database through a gateway object so the module holds rules rather than SQL. sqlpp11 removes the manual mapping - a select() over a table returns rows with named, typed members, so a rule reads like a typed query over the set - while a bare SQLite/ODBC API leaves statement preparation, binding and column mapping to the module. Choose the manual class when the team must stay on the standard library; use the typed DSL when queries are complex and compile-time checking pays for the extra dependency.
pitfalls: Returning std::vector<Row> by value copies every row; return it by move, take an output range, or stream rows through a callback, or the record set doubles in memory.
RAII is not optional: a raw sqlite3_stmt* or ODBC handle held by a module method leaks on every early return - wrap it in a handle type with a destructor.
